tests: (two further cases in the same class, same call path)

root_cause.what: the tests materialize a bench task by `git archive <task.base>`, and `task.base` for bug-a2-multi-2 is db0081275046d687e136bc2540cae78a156e7dd1 -- a commit in THIS repository's own history.
root_cause.why_ci_only: no workflow declares `fetch-depth`, so actions/checkout@v4 makes a SHALLOW clone (depth 1). The tag commit is present; the task's base commit is not. Locally the full history exists, which is why the same suite is green at the target.
root_cause.why_now: TestDuongOngTuyenCap arrived in 5388ffb (the G5.3 qualification pipeline), which is AFTER v1.6.0. Remote master is 56 commits behind local, so these tests had never run in CI -- this release tag is their first CI exposure. v1.6.0's release run was green.
root_cause.not_caused_by: today's G5.2/G5.6/early-stop work. Those changed aisef/control/{cohort,closure}.py, tests/bench/{_analyze,_runner,__main__}.py and docs; they did not touch materialize() or the task fixtures (MANIFEST.sha256 still matches byte for byte).

candidate_fixes.change: add `with: fetch-depth: 0` to actions/checkout in .github/workflows/release.yml (and tests.yml for the same reason)
candidate_fixes.note: makes CI able to resolve task.base; keeps the bench tests as real coverage. Costs a full clone per run.

candidate_fixes.change: skip the bench-materialize tests when task.base does not resolve in the checkout
candidate_fixes.note: smaller, but converts real CI coverage into a silent skip -- the exact shape this project has been burned by before (80 skips vs 19).

blocked_because: both fixes are source-changing commits, so either produces a NEW final_closure_target_sha.
